answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited stake registry: each agent must lock scarce, slashable tokens to obtain an anchor identity, and can register only a small number per unit of stake. The system tracks a signal such as completed, independently verified work; rewards and voting weight accrue gradually, while proven fraud burns the deposit and forfeits future earnings. Creating many identities therefore requires capital for each one, and an attacker risks losing it, while a harbor of unrelated accounts cannot cheaply multiply influence.
